From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Portfolio OKR — concise retro & graded rationale

Team — attaching the consolidated score workbook and a short perf vignette for the runtime objective. This is a tight ask: we need locked scores + 2-paragraph narratives for the QBR deck by EOD tomorrow so the comms and Sales brief can go out Friday morning.

Quick summary of my recommended grades (see sheet "SUMMARY"):
- Serving Runtime: 7/10 — solid latency wins but missed our throughput target by ~12% vs committed baseline.
- Model Onboarding: 8/10 — faster onboarding cadence, two successful model rollouts.
- Cost Optimization: 6/10 — caching improvements offset some spend but quantization rollout lagged.
- Observability & Rollouts: 9/10 — tracing and automatic fallback performed well in two incidents.

Content asks (clear and small):
1) Marcus — please add a one-paragraph rationale for "Serving Runtime" score with 1-2 metrics we can call out (p95 latency, throughput delta, customer impact). Attach to a reply.
2) Vivek & Laura — please flag any score you want changed (and +/− rationale) in-line.
3) All — confirm by EOD tomorrow that narrative language is publish-ready. If you can’t, tell me what’s missing.

Attachments: 2026Q4_OKR_scores_consolidated.xlsx; serving-runtime-perf-vignette.pdf

Thanks — I kept the narratives intentionally short to be exec-friendly.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product Strategy, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Irene — good framing. Quick note on Serving Runtime: I agree 7/10 might be conservative given the customer-facing reliability wins; that said, the throughput shortfall matters to committed Dedicated customers. Marcus, can you drop the metric lines Irene requested (p95, sustained throughput vs commit) so Vivek/Laura can decide whether to nudge to 7.5/10 or keep 7/10?

Also adding a customer excerpt from Acme (pasted below) that shows how the latency improvements helped their product launch. If Marcus can quantify the remaining gap, I’ll weigh in on the final.

> From: Jason Liu (Acme)
> "Latency drop on p95 made the checkout flow feel instant. Throughput ceiling still caused a visible retry at peak (BlackFriday smoke test)."

—Vivek

On Mon, Nov 8, 2026 at 10:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks, Irene — good framing. Quick note on Serving Runtime...

Folks — short justification for the Serving Runtime score (to drop into the spreadsheet and the 2-paragraph narrative):
- Primary evidence: p95 latency improved from 220ms -> 125ms across hosted API (weighted by prod traffic) after kernel selection change on 10/12.
- Throughput gap: sustained throughput at target batch sizes was 12% below our Dedicated commit at the 10k concurrent token-window during the BlackFriday sim (system-level bottleneck traced to memory bus contention on the vGPU config).
- Customer impact: Acme saw latency UX improvement but also hit a brief retry window during peak testing (see attached "serving-runtime-perf-vignette.pdf" for trace snippet).
- Recommendation: keep score at 7/10; add a mitigating action line in the narrative: "Engineering scheduled an ops-led tuning pass and kernel fallback for high-concurrency windows in the first sprint of next quarter."

If you want to raise to 7.5, the ask is: show a mitigation plan with target improvement % and timeline; otherwise 7/10 is conservative and defensible.

Marcus
Senior Engineering Manager — Serving Runtime
Attachment: serving-runtime-perf-vignette.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — I’ve read Marcus’ notes and I’m comfortable locking the scores as-is with two small edits to the narrative:
1) Add one sentence in the exec narrative noting the specific mitigation (ops tuning + kernel fallback) and expected mid-Q1 target.
2) In the customer quote slide, replace the raw Acme quote with a paraphrase that highlights the positive latency impact but acknowledges retry exposure at peak loads.

Irene — please attach the final_exec_narrative_draft.docx and I’ll approve for distribution to Sales & Exec comms. If there are no objections by EOD Friday, we publish.

Laura Bennett
